pages.title: Hyperon Crystal
pages.text: Baryons in which at least one ordinary quark has been swapped for a strange one: lambdas, sigmas, xis, packed into a lattice. Strangeness adds mass and a slow, stubborn weak decay that these crystals simply postpone. The faces are cold, the inside feels heavier than the outside, and it is never quite still.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Feeding strange matter and a sterile neutrino through the synchrotron, I tried to coax strange quarks into ordinary baryons. Tachyon crystal stretched the decay clock long enough for the hyperons to settle into a lattice instead of decaying.
